Powerful.jl

Fast, composable power system simulation in Julia

Powerful.jl is a modern power systems analysis package designed for speed, flexibility, and ease of use. It provides efficient implementations of power flow analysis and time-domain simulation with support for GPU acceleration and automatic differentiation.

Key Features

  • Modern API: DifferentialEquations.jl-style interface with composable problem/algorithm separation
  • High Performance: Sparse matrix methods, GPU acceleration, and zero-allocation residual evaluation
  • Multiple Formulations: Power injection (P-θ, Q-V) and current injection (Ir-Vr, Ii-Vi) formulations
  • Flexible Solvers: Native Newton-Raphson, Fast Decoupled, and NonlinearSolve.jl backend
  • Automatic Differentiation: ForwardDiff.jl integration for sensitivity analysis and optimization
  • Island Detection: Automatic handling of disconnected network components
  • GPU Support: CUDA acceleration for large-scale systems
  • Time-Domain Simulation: Dynamic models with differential-algebraic equation (DAE) solvers

Quick Start

Installation

using Pkg
Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/sensl/Powerful.jl")

Basic Power Flow

using Powerful
using PowerFlowData

# Load system data
case = PowerFlowData.parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys = SystemModel(case)

# Create problem and solve
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())

# Check convergence
if sol.converged
    println("Converged in $(sol.iterations) iterations")
    println("Final residual: $(sol.residual_norm)")
end

# Extract results
v = get_var(sol, :Bus, :v, 1)  # Bus 1 voltage magnitude
θ = get_var(sol, :Bus, :θ, 1)  # Bus 1 voltage angle

Advanced Features

# Current injection formulation (better conditioned)
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, CurrentInjection())
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())

# Fast Decoupled (2-3x faster for large transmission networks)
sol = solve(prob, FastDecoupledXB())

# Robust solver for difficult cases
sol = solve(prob, RobustNewton())

# GPU acceleration (requires CUDA + CUDSS)
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson(linear_solver=CUDSSSolver()))

# AMD reordering for sparse factorization
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection(); addressing=AMDAddressing())
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())

Generating Reports

using DataFrames

# Collect results as table (automatically converts to physical units)
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)
df = DataFrame(bus_data)

# Print formatted report
report = build_powerflow_report(sol)
println(format_text(report))

Architecture Overview

Powerful.jl uses a layered architecture that separates concerns:

  1. Foundation: Type system, metadata, traits
  2. Indexing: External IDs ↔ internal indices ↔ DAE addresses
  3. Models: Component implementations (buses, loads, generators, branches)
  4. System: Coordinates models into unified DAE system
  5. Solvers: Numerical methods using DAE interface

This design enables:

  • Extensibility: Easy to add new models and solvers
  • Performance: Type-stable code with compiler optimizations
  • Correctness: Clear separation prevents coupling bugs
  • Flexibility: Different formulations use same model implementations

Command-Line Interface

Powerful.jl includes a unified CLI for fast development:

# Power flow analysis (daemon auto-starts if needed)
./bin/powerful cases/ieee14.raw --output report.txt

# Run tests
./bin/powerful test                    # Run all tests
./bin/powerful test test/my_test.jl    # Run specific test file

# Run Julia code
./bin/powerful run examples/tds_flat_run.jl

See bin/README.md for complete CLI documentation.
